subject: Problem when running non library version of GGIR

messages.author: 5636dac60e2efbc1
messages.subject: Problem when running non library version of GGIR
parts:
Hello,

With the new updates to parallel processing, I was having trouble on my machine when I wanted to run the code when it was downloaded from git (NOT from R studio library, install.packages).

The problem occurred at this line in g.part1 (line 219), g.part2 (line 79), g.part3 (line 55) and g.part 5 (line 96):

output_list =foreach::foreach(i=f0:f1, .packages = 'GGIR', .errorhandling='pass') %myinfix% { # the process can take easily 1 minute per file, so probably there is a time gain by doing it parallel

I found that if I removed the .packages = 'GGIR' argument, then it would run fine, but I suspect this may cause a problem for parallel processing.

Does anybody know if there is a way to check to see if you are using the library version of GGIR or a git downloaded version and then to run this line appropriately so it can work for either way?

Thanks, Matt

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Problem when running non library version of GGIR
parts:
Hi Matt,
I noticed that too. When foreach is used to do the parallel processing it expects that every function called from within the foreach loop is part of an installed package.
The temporary solution I found was to leave .packages = 'GGIR' inside the foreach call, but to rebuild the package with every update of the code. 
I have not had time yet to investigate this, but surely there must me better solution as there are many packages that rely on foreach.
Best, Vincent
